narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and the assessment found a 63% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a level of uncertainty high enough to result in a denial. This decision was shaped by several aspects of your financial profile, and understanding them may help you take steps toward a successful application in the future.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the length of the loan you requested: 48 months, which is more than double the average of roughly 19 months seen among applicants who were approved. A longer loan term means the bank is exposed to risk over a much greater period of time, and combined with the size of your request — 7,685 DM, compared to an average of about 2,887 DM among approved applicants — the overall commitment you are asking the bank to make is substantially larger than what is typically seen in successful applications. These two elements together paint a picture of a high-exposure loan that gave the model significant pause.

The second most important factor was the status of your checking account, which currently shows a negative balance. While it is true that nearly 20% of approved applicants also had accounts in the red, the combination of a negative balance with such a long and large loan request amplified the concern considerably. A healthy or positive checking account balance signals financial stability, and its absence here reinforced the risk signal already raised by the loan's terms.

On a more positive note, the fact that you have a guarantor on your application actually worked in your favor, nudging the assessment slightly toward a more favorable outcome. Having someone willing to back your loan is a meaningful sign of accountability, and it is one of the stronger positive signals in your profile — though it was not enough to outweigh the concerns raised by the loan duration and your account status.

Your credit history — showing all debts paid at the bank — is held by only about 3% of approved applicants, which is an unusual profile that the model may not have found reassuring in the way you might expect. Additionally, renting your home rather than owning it places you in a smaller segment of approved borrowers, where 76% own their residence.

As a next step, you may want to consider whether the loan amount or duration could be reduced, as bringing these closer to more typical ranges could meaningfully improve your chances. Working to bring your checking account into a positive balance before reapplying would also strengthen your profile considerably. Speaking with a financial advisor or a bank representative directly could help you identify the most practical path forward given your specific circumstances.
